Subject: Post-call: MAP draft - data handling & retention milestones (MedSys)

Hi Helen / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. High-level recap and proposed next steps focused only on the MAP milestone for data handling / compliance so we can align on scope before the legal/contract review. I attached the MAP draft (Redwood_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) with the section we discussed highlighted.

Key discovery notes (from our call):
- Data types: inbound clinical transcripts + assorted patient identifiers (PHI) and provider notes (PII).
- Retention target: company preference is 7 years for primary PHI records; shorter windows (1–3 years) acceptable for derived telemetry/logs.
- Auditability: need immutable audit trails for access and admin changes; exportable CSV for e-discovery.
- Encryption: customer-managed KMS preferred for keys; HSM option for private deployments.
- De-identification: they plan to run redaction pipeline in front of ingestion but asked whether Redwood can additionally support token-level suppression for outputs.

Proposed MAP milestone (data handling & compliance):
- Milestone: Confirm retention & logging requirements
  - Owner: MedSys legal (Kimberly) + Redwood Solutions (Monica)
  - Target: 2026-11-27 (initial alignment)
  - Dependency: SOC2 attestation + DPA template review

- Milestone: Production data path & encryption model (KMS/HSM)
  - Owner: MedSys infra (Rajiv) + Redwood infra (Rishi)
  - Target: 2026-12-08
  - Dependency: Private deployment options / network review if needed

- Milestone: PHI handling / redaction approach and acceptance tests
  - Owner: MedSys security + Redwood CS (Monica)
  - Target: 2026-12-15
  - Dependency: sample dataset or redaction spec from MedSys

Target close date we discussed on the call: 2026-12-18. If we can get Kimberly and Rajiv to confirm the milestones above and the dependency list, I will circulate an updated MAP (v2) and a focused checklist for the legal team.

Open asks for MedSys to confirm in reply:
1) Is 7 years retention required for all PHI or only the canonical patient records?
2) Will MedSys share a short redaction spec or a 1–2MB sample file for acceptance testing?
3) Who is the formal security/legal reviewer (I noted Kimberly — please confirm).

I copied Monica and Rishi here to propose technical options and to pick up SOC2 / DPA items.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP section highlighted)

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks, Priyom — helpful recap. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions from our side:

Answers:
- Retention: 7 years is required for our canonical PHI clinical records. Telemetry/logging can be shorter, ideally 18 months by default.
- Security reviewer: Kimberly Tran (cc'd) will own the DPA and legal sign-off.

Clarifying questions / asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a sample DPA clause that explicitly references retention windows per data class and an exportable audit trail format?
2) Does Redwood support automatic redaction on ingest, or is the recommended pattern to run a pre-ingest pipeline managed by MedSys? We want to understand both options and any QA requirements.
3) Please provide SOC2 report and most recent pen-test summary for our internal reviewers (we will share with Kimberly and infra).

Also: Rajiv and I will confirm whether we can provide a reduced sample dataset (de-identified) for acceptance testing by tomorrow EOD.

Appreciate the clear owner assignments — Kimberly will coordinate with our procurement/legal team for the DPA timeline.

Best,
Helen

Hi Helen / team —

Thanks — I pulled together the technical answers and attached two artifacts: SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf and retention_policy_summary.xlsx. Answers below are intentionally pragmatic so we can finalize the MAP milestone language.

1) DPA / retention clause: we can provide a draft DPA clause that enumerates retention per data class. Typical pattern we use in MAPs: default log retention = 12 months (configurable), PHI canonical retention = customer-configurable up to 7+ years for Dedicated/Private. We will include an exportable audit CSV schema (columns: timestamp, event_type, actor_id, resource, action, outcome).

2) Redaction options:
- Pre-ingest (recommended): MedSys runs redaction/de-identification before sending data to Redwood. This keeps the ingestion pipeline under your control and is the simplest from a compliance standpoint.
- Ingest-time suppression: Redwood can implement token-level suppression rules and masking at inference time for outputs; however, automated full-PHI redaction on ingest is not a managed feature out-of-the-box — we can build a supported integration for an additional engineering scope (dependency: sample dataset + redaction spec).

3) SOC2 / pen test: attached SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf. For penetration test summaries we typically share an executive summary; a full report requires an NDA in some cases — happy to work through Kimberly on that.

Proposed updated MAP items (I will fold these into v2):
- Deliverable: Redwood to provide DPA sample clause + audit CSV schema
  - Owner: Redwood Legal (Lauren) + Monica (solutions)
  - Due: 2026-11-24
  - Notes: Kimberly to confirm any redlines by 2026-11-30
\- Deliverable: SOC2 & security artefacts delivered to MedSys
  - Owner: Redwood Compliance (Lauren)
  - Due: 2026-11-20
\- Deliverable: Technical design for KMS/HSM and network model
  - Owner: Rishi (Redwood infra) + Rajiv (MedSys)
  - Due: 2026-12-03
\Attachments: SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf; retention_policy_summary.xlsx

If it's helpful, I can set up a 30-minute technical deep dive with Rishi + Rajiv next week to lock down the KMS/network options.

Thanks,
Monica
